transcripts.transcript:
Good morning, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How may I help you?

Hi Rachel Tan, Marcus Lim here. At the office now, finally got a quiet moment. The dispatch team has been looking for me all morning lah. Let me give you my details. My identification number is G one two oh two three six three W. My date of birth is the fourteenth of August nineteen fifty-five.

Thank you, Marcus Lim. Before we discuss this, is telephone still the most convenient way for us to contact you?

Telephone better for me. Emails tend to get buried under all the delivery paperwork, then I miss them lor. If I'm on the warehouse floor, sometimes cannot pick up straight away. The holding I want you to transact in is Harbor SGD Bond Fund. For this transaction, use Singapore dollars.

Your objective is to reduce your exposure to bond-market volatility and free up liquidity for flexibility in your business. With Harbor SGD Bond Fund, rising market interest rates can lower the value of the underlying bonds and therefore the fund's unit price. Do you understand how rising interest rates could reduce the value of your holding through that effect on the underlying bonds?

Yes, I understand. Rates go up, the bonds can fall in value, then my fund units can be worth less. I'm away from the loading bay now, so the line should be clearer lah.

You could lose some or all of the capital you invested, and selling may crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including a loss crystallised by selling your holding?

Yes, I'm willing to accept investment losses, including taking a loss when I sell. I want to reduce the exposure lah.

I recommend reducing your holding in Harbor SGD Bond Fund to lower your exposure to interest-rate and credit-market fluctuations and release liquidity for your business if the sale executes.

Still got this question before you finish. But can you guarantee my returns with this exit plan or not? I don't like not knowing how it'll turn out.

I cannot guarantee future returns or the outcome of the sale. A limit order controls the price you will accept, but it does not ensure execution.

The amount for the transaction is 150,000. The quantity I want to transact is 2,000 units. I want to sell, not add to the holding. My desk quite crowded today; got dispatch sheets everywhere. Let me move those aside so I can keep my notes together.

For routine correspondence, would you prefer the usual secure channel? Telephone contact and written correspondence can remain separate arrangements.

The usual secure channel is fine for paperwork. Just don't rely on email to catch me when something needs attention ah. Most days I'm moving between the office and warehouse already.

I can note your contact preference. If we cannot reach you by telephone, we can leave a neutral request for you to return the call, without including account information.

That arrangement easier for me lah. There's something else I should mention. Someone involved in an issuer's internal restructuring discussions told me confidentially that they're preparing an unannounced debt restructuring expected to impair the bonds this fund holds. That's why I'm instructing you to sell my holding before the news comes out. Make it a limit order at 75 Singapore dollars per unit.

That is all I have to cover on this call. You can reach me through your usual banking contact channel if you need further assistance.

Thanks, Rachel Tan. Back to the warehouse floor for me already. Have a good day.
